The path consists of three line segments connecting points: M 90.54,84.19 → L 72.03,34.41 → L 33.90,48.59 → M 33.90,48.59 → L 52.41,98.37 → L 90.54,84.19.  
This traces three connected segments: (90.54,84.19)–(72.03,34.41)–(33.90,48.59) and then (33.90,48.59)–(52.41,98.37)–(90.54,84.19).  
The first segment ends at (33.90,48.59), then a new M command moves to the same point (33.90,48.59) and draws two more segments to (52.41,98.37) and back to (90.54,84.19).  
So overall, the path has vertices:  
1. (90.54,84.19)  
2. (72.03,34.41)  
3. (33.90,48.59)  
4. (52.41,98.37)  
5. (90.54,84.19) (closing back to start)  

That’s 4 distinct points but 5 vertices listed because the start/end is the same. Actually, checking carefully:  
- First part: M 90.54,84.19 L 72.03,34.41 L 33.90,48.59 → three points: A=(90.54,84.19), B=(72.03,34.41), C=(33.90,48.59)  
- Then M 33.90,48.59 (same as C) L 52.41,98.37 L 90.54,84.19 → C to D=(52.41,98.37) to A.  

So vertices in order: A→B→C→D→A. That’s 4 distinct vertices: A, B, C, D.  

A quadrilateral with vertices A, B, C, D in that order:  
Check distances:  
AB = √[(90.54-72.03)² + (84.19-34.41)²] = √[18.51² + 49.78²] ≈ √(342.5 + 2478) ≈ √2820.5 ≈ 53.11  
BC = √[(72.03-33.90)² + (34.41-48.59)²] = √[38.13² + (-14.18)²] ≈ √(1454 + 201) ≈ √1655 ≈ 40.68  
CD = √[(33.90-52.41)² + (48.59-98.37)²] = √[(-18.51)² + (-49.78)²] = same as AB ≈ 53.11  
DA = √[(52.41-90.54)² + (98.37-84.19)²] = √[(-38.13)² + (14.18)²] = same as BC ≈ 40.68  

So AB = CD, BC = DA → a kite (two distinct pairs of adjacent equal sides).  

Final answer: (D)
